title: Gibbs sampling, exact coupling and finite-error certificates

items.title: Finite-spin random-scan heat-bath update
items.statement:
Input a finite nonempty site set $V$, a finite nonempty spin set $S$ with a fixed total order $s_1\prec\cdots\prec s_r$, a strictly positive finite weight $w:S^V\to(0,\infty)$, an initial configuration $x_0\in S^V$, an integer $t\geq0$, a site schedule $i_1,\ldots,i_t\in V$, numbers $u_1,\ldots,u_t\in[0,1]$, and a finite family of observables $f_1,\ldots,f_m:S^V\to\mathbb R$ (the family may be empty). Put $Z=\sum_{x\in S^V}w(x)$ and $\pi(x)=w(x)/Z$. For $i\in V$, an exterior configuration $\eta\in S^{V\setminus\{i\}}$, and $s\in S$, let $\eta^{i,s}\in S^V$ agree with $\eta$ away from $i$ and have spin $s$ at $i$, and set
$$q_i(s\mid\eta)=\frac{w(\eta^{i,s})}{\sum_{a\in S}w(\eta^{i,a})}.$$
The denominator is finite and strictly positive. For $k=1,\ldots,t$, set $\eta=x_{k-1}|_{V\setminus\{i_k\}}$, put $c_0=0$ and $c_j=\sum_{\ell=1}^j q_{i_k}(s_\ell\mid\eta)$, and replace the spin at $i_k$ by the first $s_j$ for which $u_k<c_j$; when $u_k=1$, replace it by $s_r$. Leave every other spin unchanged to obtain $x_k$. Thus the intervals are $[c_{j-1},c_j)$ for $j<r$ and $[c_{r-1},1]$ for $j=r$. Return the trajectory $(x_0,\ldots,x_t)$ and the values $f_a(x_k)$ for $a=1,\ldots,m$ and $k=0,\ldots,t$. For the random-scan heat-bath chain, take the $i_k$ independently uniform on $V$ and the $u_k$ independently uniform on $[0,1]$, with all site and uniform draws mutually independent. The procedure makes no independence claim about successive configurations or observable values.

references.title: Sascha Friedli and Yvan Velenik, Statistical Mechanics of Lattice Systems: A Concrete Mathematical Introduction
references.locator: Chapter 3, §3.1, printed pp. 80–82: finite Gibbs weights and conditional distributions. The procedure below is defined for arbitrary finite positive weights.

references.title: David A. Levin, Yuval Peres, and Elizabeth L. Wilmer, Markov Chains and Mixing Times, second edition
references.locator: Chapter 3, §3.3.2, printed pp. 42–43, and Chapter 25, §25.2, printed pp. 348–350: finite single-site conditional resampling and the Ising heat-bath randomization.

items.title: Finite Dobrushin bound for random-scan heat-bath sampling
items.statement:
Let $V$ be a finite nonempty set with $n=|V|$, let $S$ be a finite nonempty set, and let $w:S^V\to(0,\infty)$ be a finite positive weight. Let $\pi(x)=w(x)/\sum_{y\in S^V}w(y)$ and let $q_i(s\mid\eta)$ be the one-site conditional law defined by the finite-spin heat-bath update. For $i\ne j$, define
$$c_{ij}=\sup_{\substack{\eta,\eta'\in S^{V\setminus\{i\}}\\\eta_k=\eta'_k\ \text{for all }k\ne j}}\frac12\sum_{s\in S}|q_i(s\mid\eta)-q_i(s\mid\eta')|,\qquad c_{ii}=0.$$
Assume that for some $c\in[0,1)$, both $\max_i\sum_jc_{ij}\leq c$ and $\max_j\sum_ic_{ij}\leq c$. Define $P(x,y)$ as the one-step transition probability of the random-scan heat-bath update, and let $X_t$ be the resulting chain started at $x\in S^V$. For every integer $t\geq0$,
$$\left\|\mathcal L_x(X_t)-\pi\right\|_{\rm TV}\leq n\left(1-\frac{1-c}{n}\right)^t\leq n\exp\!\left(-\frac{(1-c)t}{n}\right),\qquad \|\mu-\nu\|_{\rm TV}:=\frac12\sum_{z\in S^V}|\mu(z)-\nu(z)|.$$
Consequently, for every $a\leq b$ and every $f:S^V\to[a,b]$,
$$\left|\mathbb E_x f(X_t)-\sum_{z\in S^V}\pi(z)f(z)\right|\leq(b-a)n\exp\!\left(-\frac{(1-c)t}{n}\right).$$
This is a deterministic bias certificate for the expectation under the specified finite model. It is not a per-realization guarantee, an independent-sample confidence bound, or a claim about critical systems.

references.title: Sascha Friedli and Yvan Velenik, Statistical Mechanics of Lattice Systems: A Concrete Mathematical Introduction
references.locator: Chapter 6, §6.5.2, Theorem 6.31 and equations (6.37)–(6.40), printed pp. 268–269 (PDF pp. 285–286). That theorem concerns an infinite-volume uniqueness criterion; the finite-time chain estimate below is proved locally.

items.title: Additive composition of finite sampling error budgets
items.statement:
Let $\theta,\theta_T,m,\widehat m,\widetilde m\in\mathbb R$ be, respectively, a target quantity, a finite/truncated target, the exact mean under the specified finite sampling law, one realized sample statistic, and its rounded computed value. Let $\epsilon_{\rm tr},\epsilon_{\rm mix},\epsilon_{\rm stat},\epsilon_{\rm arith}\geq0$ have the same units as these quantities. If
$$|\theta_T-\theta|\leq\epsilon_{\rm tr},\qquad |m-\theta_T|\leq\epsilon_{\rm mix},\qquad |\widehat m-m|\leq\epsilon_{\rm stat},\qquad |\widetilde m-\widehat m|\leq\epsilon_{\rm arith},$$
then
$$|\widetilde m-\theta|\leq\epsilon_{\rm tr}+\epsilon_{\rm mix}+\epsilon_{\rm stat}+\epsilon_{\rm arith}.$$
Here the statistical inequality is conditional on the explicitly supplied realized-error event; the statement assigns no probability to that event. The four terms respectively record truncation, finite-sampling bias or mixing, statistical deviation, and arithmetic rounding. No term may be omitted unless its corresponding error is separately proved to be zero.

references.title: David A. Levin, Yuval Peres, and Elizabeth L. Wilmer, Markov Chains and Mixing Times, second edition
references.locator: Chapter 4, §§4.1–4.2, printed pp. 47–49 (PDF pp. 62–64): total variation as a metric and finite-law error comparisons. The scalar four-term decomposition below is proved locally.

items.title: Monotone coupling from the past for finite ferromagnetic Ising weights
items.statement:
Input a finite nonempty set $V$, a set $E\subseteq[V]^2$ of unordered pairs of distinct sites, finite dimensionless couplings $K_e\geq0$, finite dimensionless fields $h_i\in\mathbb R$, and a two-sided iid stream $(I_s,U_s)_{s\in\mathbb Z}$ in which $I_s$ is uniform on $V$, $U_s$ is uniform on $[0,1]$, and all these variables are mutually independent. On $\Omega=\{-1,+1\}^V$, define $\sigma\leq\tau$ by $\sigma_i\leq\tau_i$ for every $i\in V$, using $-1<+1$; its least and greatest elements are $\mathbf{-}$ and $\mathbf{+}$. For the finite-spin heat-bath update, use the total sampling order $+1\prec-1$, which is distinct from $\leq$. Define the strictly positive finite weight
$$w(\sigma)=\exp\!\left(\sum_{\{i,j\}\in E}K_{\{i,j\}}\sigma_i\sigma_j+\sum_{i\in V}h_i\sigma_i\right).$$
At time $s$, let $F_s:\Omega\to\Omega$ be the one-site finite-spin heat-bath update at site $I_s$ with uniform value $U_s$, leaving every other spin unchanged; explicitly, site $i$ is set to $+1$ exactly when
$$U_s<\frac{\exp(H_i(\eta))}{\exp(H_i(\eta))+\exp(-H_i(\eta))},\qquad H_i(\eta)=h_i+\sum_{\{i,j\}\in E}K_{\{i,j\}}\eta_j,$$
where $\eta$ is the exterior configuration at $i$, and otherwise is set to $-1$. For $T=1,2,4,\ldots$, initialize lower and upper configurations at time $-T$ to $\mathbf{-}$ and $\mathbf{+}$, respectively, and apply in chronological order the same stored maps $F_{-T+1},\ldots,F_0$ to both. If their time-zero outputs agree, return that common configuration. Otherwise double $T$ and replay all maps in the enlarged interval, reusing the already stored maps at every overlapping time. This is a random procedure; no finite running-time bound is part of its definition.
items.strategy: Operational doubling procedure with a stored shared past stream.

references.title: David A. Levin, Yuval Peres, and Elizabeth L. Wilmer, Markov Chains and Mixing Times, second edition
references.locator: Chapter 25, §§25.1–25.2, printed pp. 347–354 (PDF pp. 363–369): monotone Ising heat-bath updates, shared past randomness, doubling, and runtime caveats.

items.title: Exactness and almost-sure termination of finite monotone CFTP
items.statement:
For every finite nonempty $V$, finite interaction set $E\subseteq[V]^2$, finite couplings $K_e\geq0$, and finite fields $h_i\in\mathbb R$ in the monotone coupling-from-the-past procedure, the doubling algorithm terminates almost surely under its stated iid seed law. Its returned configuration has exactly the Gibbs distribution
$$\pi(\sigma)=\frac{w(\sigma)}{\sum_{\tau\in\{-1,+1\}^V}w(\tau)},\qquad w(\sigma)=\exp\!\left(\sum_{\{i,j\}\in E}K_{\{i,j\}}\sigma_i\sigma_j+\sum_{i\in V}h_i\sigma_i\right).$$
Let $P(x,y)$ be the one-update random-scan heat-bath transition probability, and for every integer $m\geq0$ let $P^m$ denote its $m$-step transition matrix. Define total variation on $\Omega=\{-1,+1\}^V$ by $\|\mu-\nu\|_{\rm TV}=\frac12\sum_{x\in\Omega}|\mu(x)-\nu(x)|$. This exactness claim gives no bound on expected or worst-case runtime.

references.title: David A. Levin, Yuval Peres, and Elizabeth L. Wilmer, Markov Chains and Mixing Times, second edition
references.locator: Chapter 25, §§25.1–25.3, printed pp. 347–355 (PDF pp. 363–371): monotone coupling from the past and the need to reuse the same maps on overlapping horizons. The local proof below supplies its finite positive-block termination argument and stationary-law identification.

items.title: Finite Potts Swendsen–Wang update
items.statement: Input a finite simple graph $G=(V,E)$, an integer $Q\geq2$, finite activities $v_e\geq0$ for $e\in E$, and a spin configuration $\sigma:V\to[Q]$, using the Potts and FK conventions of the finite Potts/FK weight definition. For each edge $e=\{u,v\}$, if $\sigma(u)\ne\sigma(v)$ set $e$ absent. If $\sigma(u)=\sigma(v)$, draw an independent uniform $U_e\in[0,1]$ and place $e$ in $A$ exactly when $U_e<v_e/(1+v_e)$. For each connected component of $(V,A)$, draw an independent uniform $U_C\in[0,1]$ and assign its vertices the common color $1+\lfloor Q U_C\rfloor$, with the value $Q$ used when $U_C=1$. Return the resulting spin configuration $\sigma'$. The finite graph has finitely many edges and components, so the procedure uses finitely many draws and operations. At $v_e=0$ the edge is never activated; finite $v_e$ ensures the activation probability is less than one.
items.strategy: Two finite conditional draws from the Potts/FK joint model.

references.title: Geoffrey R. Grimmett, The Random-Cluster Model
references.locator: §§2.2–2.3, printed pp. 6–9 (PDF pp. 5–8), and §8.3 (PDF pp. 38–39): finite Potts/FK coupling and the two-stage Swendsen–Wang update.

references.title: Hugo Duminil-Copin, Geometric Representations of Lattice Spin Models, Cours Peccot lecture notes

items.title: Finite Swendsen–Wang update preserves the Potts law
items.statement: For a finite simple graph $G=(V,E)$, integer $Q\geq2$, and finite activities $v_e\geq0$, let $\pi_P(\sigma)=w_P(\sigma)/Z_P$ be the normalized finite Potts law and let the Swendsen–Wang update be the two-stage procedure of activating equal-spin edges with probabilities $v_e/(1+v_e)$ and independently recoloring each resulting component uniformly from $[Q]$. Its transition kernel preserves $\pi_P$. The procedure always terminates after finitely many edge and component operations. No irreducibility, uniqueness, convergence-rate, or critical-mixing claim is made.

references.title: Geoffrey R. Grimmett, The Random-Cluster Model
references.locator: §2.3, printed pp. 7–9 (PDF pp. 6–8), and §8.3 (PDF pp. 38–39): the finite joint Potts/FK law and Swendsen–Wang update.

references.title: Hugo Duminil-Copin, Geometric Representations of Lattice Spin Models, Cours Peccot lecture notes

title: Gibbs sampling, exact coupling and finite-error certificates — Examples

items.title: A finite Metropolis chain can equilibrate within a well and remain far from equilibrium
items.statement:
Assume AC. Fix $\beta>0$ in reciprocal-energy units and a finite barrier height $B>0$ in the corresponding energy unit, so $\beta B$ is dimensionless; put $\epsilon=e^{-\beta B}\in(0,1)$, and let the five states be $\Omega=\{L_0,L_1,H,R_0,R_1\}$. Equip $\Omega$ with the discrete metric $\rho(x,y)=\mathbf1_{\{x\ne y\}}$, whose Borel sigma-algebra is $2^\Omega:=\{A:A\subseteq\Omega\}$; the target and proposal are defined on the measurable carrier $(\Omega,2^\Omega)$. The energies are $E(L_0)=E(L_1)=E(R_0)=E(R_1)=0$ and $E(H)=B$, so the Gibbs law is $\pi(x)=e^{-\beta E(x)}/(4+\epsilon)$. Let $Q$ be the symmetric proposal matrix specified by
$$Q(L_i,L_i)=Q(R_i,R_i)=\frac12,\quad Q(L_i,L_{1-i})=Q(R_i,R_{1-i})=\frac14,\quad Q(L_i,H)=Q(R_i,H)=\frac14\quad(i=0,1),$$
and $Q(H,x)=1/4$ for $x\in\{L_0,L_1,R_0,R_1\}$, with all other entries zero. Each row sums to one. Apply the Metropolis–Hastings procedure with target $\pi$ and proposal $Q$, and denote its transition matrix by $P$. Write $L=\{L_0,L_1\}$ for the left well and, for each $t\in\mathbb Z_{\geq0}$, define
$$d(t)=\max_{x\in\Omega}\|P^t(x,\cdot)-\pi\|_{\rm TV},\qquad \|\mu-\nu\|_{\rm TV}=\frac12\sum_{x\in\Omega}|\mu(x)-\nu(x)|.$$
The Gibbs law is invariant, but the chain started with law $\pi(\cdot\mid L)$ has probability $(1-\epsilon/4)^t$ of making no exit from $L$ during its first $t$ steps. Conditional on no exit, its two-state within-well transition flips between $L_0$ and $L_1$ with probability $1/(4-\epsilon)$; the conditional stationary law within the well is uniform, and from either state its within-well total-variation error after $t$ such updates is at most $\frac12((2-\epsilon)/(4-\epsilon))^t\leq2^{-t-1}$. Nevertheless,
$$d(t)\geq(1-\epsilon/4)^t-\frac{2}{4+\epsilon}\geq\frac14\qquad\text{for every integer }0\leq t\leq\lfloor\epsilon^{-1}\rfloor.$$
Thus the conventional worst-start mixing time $t_{\rm mix}(1/8):=\min\{t\in\mathbb Z_{\geq0}:d(t)\leq1/8\}$ exceeds $\lfloor e^{\beta B}\rfloor$, even though the chain can equilibrate quickly within one well. This is an exact finite mathematical example; it reports no simulated or measured data.
